title: Apple Spent Billions Buying Back Its Own Stock
text: Home Phone Apple Spent Billions Buying Back Its Own Stock Apple Spent Billions Buying Back Its Own Stock by - Charles Ifeanyi on - December 31, 2018 Apple has overcome a turbulent year of trading in the US stock market. U., Recording both important gains (up to $ 232.07 per share) as significant losses (as low as $ 146.83), from its debut value of $ 172.26 on January 2. , 2018 at its current price of ~ $ 156 per share. And while several mishaps (including reports of a lower iPhone demand for stellar, reduced production and the pretentious commercial war between the U.S. and China), have ultimately played In the AAPL wild race this year, a new report published by Business Insider on Friday highlights (with an interesting detail) Apple's strategy of buying "odiously" shares of its own shares in 2018, noting that in the first Three quarters of the year, Apple spent almost $ 63 billion in the repurchase of its own shares. "Throughout the first nine months of 2018, Apple spent $ 62.9 billion in stock repurchases," the publication notes, adding that the "record and surprising sum" is equal to the total revenue of the technology giant during the quarter ending on September 30, 2018 .. A bad investment Interestingly, several economists who spoke with Business Insider pointed out that the traditional purpose of stock repurchases is "to increase the price of shares and make gains per action look better." This may imply that Apple, which purchased several millions of its AAPL shares for up to $ 222.07 each, may have overestimated the volatility and enhancement of its actions in the short and long term. As noted in a separate report from The Wall Street Journal that was also published on Friday, Apple's shares have lost approximately 30 percent of its maximum value of $ 232.07 per share on October 3, its Current price of ~ $ 156 per share as of December 28. . This means that the estimated value of 6.7 percent of pending shares that Apple bought for almost $ 63 billion now has a value of around $ 53.8 billion (as of Wednesday's historic operations), the which represents an estimated total loss of about $ 9 billion. Or a master plan? As reported previously, 2018 saw Apple become the first corporation of billions of dollars worldwide. And while market capitalization of the technology giant remains comfortably around around $ 750 billion, it's definitely worth noting that Apple is probably not too upset about losses. The iPhone manufacturer boldly announced its plans to repurchase a large part of its AAPL shares last December, and CEO Tim Cook stated that the measure will be "good for the economy", exposing it voluntarily and arbitrarily at Technological giant to the possibility of losses along the lines of (or even worse than) it has already suffered. But while Apple can certainly afford the loss of billions of dollars without interrupting its global results or its global operations, its current repurchase strategy is not sustainable, according to the sources cited by WSJ. "If they made an acquisition that diminished so much in value, people would be in arms," ​​said Nell Minow, vice president of ValueEdge Advisors, adding that Apple's repurchase, its main investment in terms of dollars and cents this year , declined "so much, so fast." However, what is perhaps the most interesting of all is that even in spite of these losses, Apple is ready and preparing to buy more shares of AAPL in 2019, for a sum of + $ 70 billion, of In accordance with its repurchase program of $ 100 billion. And yet, with so many new Apple products and technologies still to be unveiled in preparation for its launch in 2019 and beyond, it is reasonable to assume that AAPL will eventually compensate for all of these losses, and then some, anyway Tags
